patterns.what_worked: The client's own spell data (the wowsims repos' generated tables) plus wowhead's per-version pages settled every per-family spell id WITHOUT guessing - including two ids the filed residual had wrong (the Forever client has the Bestial Wrath, the Rapid Fire, the Raptor Strike and the Aimed Shot; it lacks only the Steady Shot and the Kill Command). The per-family table plus one unified re-point loop made the guide and the HUD share a single owner, so the agreement pin is structural rather than a coincidence.
patterns.what_was_hard: A sim's generated spell table is not proof of ABSENCE (the TBC table also omits Rapid Fire and the Bestial Wrath, which the TBC client does have) - the absence claims needed a second, independent source (wowhead's version page) before a slot was dropped. The shared hud_state fixture also had to grow a per-family spell option, because one shared spell table cannot model seven clients' rank ladders.
patterns.skill_gap: Proving a slot is ABSENT needs two independent sources, not one; and a mutant that survives may be an equivalent mutant rather than a missing pin - both need to be said out loud in the report instead of being quietly dropped.
